players.product: power management passive components (resistors, capacitors) for Rubin boards

quarterly_data.signal: Fourth-quarter 2025 results: revenue of $801 million, slightly above the midpoint of the $790 million guidance and 1.3% higher than the third quarter, driven by a growing broad-based business in industrial power and AI-related power applications, with the quarter's growth coming entirely from Asia (+3.6%). Versus 2024, revenue increased 12%, driven by an 11% increase in volume. Gross profit was $157 million for a gross margin of 19.6% (Newport fab drag approximately 130 basis points, plus elevated metals and material costs); EBITDA was $70 million for an EBITDA margin of 8.8%; GAAP EPS was 1¢.
quarterly_data.figure: $801 million revenue (1.3% higher than Q3; revenue increased 12% vs 2024); gross margin of 19.6%; EBITDA margin of 8.8%

quarterly_data.signal: Fourth-quarter orders were at a three-year high across all main product technologies except capacitors, and at three-year highs in the OEM, distribution and EMS channels; backlog grew nearly 14% with both semis and passives contributing, and in Asia strong AI-related demand once again drove order growth. Book-to-bill was 1.2 (up from the 1.15 run rate shared in October), with semis at 1.27 and passives at 1.13; backlog at quarter end was $1.3 billion or 4.9 months. Management said the January '26 book-to-bill is building momentum, and that the solid book-to-bill and faster backlog development support its view that revenue will increase each quarter of 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: semis book-to-bill 1.27, passives 1.13; backlog 4.9 months; backlog grew nearly 14%

quarterly_data.signal: AI power is a growing driver: revenue in the 'other' category grew 10.6% versus the third quarter, primarily as customers ramp up production for new products to support AI power management applications, and order intake grew on increased production of AI servers and extended component lead times across the industry. "A number of customers are actively adding Vishay to the bill of materials in AI-related applications for both semiconductors and passives." Design activity covers multiphase DC to DC converter modules, chipset multiphase power and AI optical modules, Vishay is working with customers on 800 volts power management applications, and designs supporting AI infrastructure are moving to mass production. EMS revenue increased 1.4% on gains in Asia related to AI power, and Asian distributors are replenishing backlogs in anticipation of stronger AI demand forecast for 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: other category revenue grew 10.6% versus the third quarter; EMS revenue increased 1.4%

quarterly_data.signal: First-quarter 2026 guidance (the CFO worded it 'For 2026, revenues are expected to be between $800 million and $830 million' while guiding the quarter against Q4 and the Lunar New Year): Asia revenue lower than Q4 due to the Lunar New Year with The Americas and Europe making up the difference, and sequential revenue increases expected in each of the five key growth segments, including AI computing. Gross margin guided at 19.9%, plus or minus 50 basis points, including tariff impacts and higher input costs; the Newport drag is expected at 50 to 75 basis points, with Newport exiting quarter one gross-profit neutral and accretive thereafter. Depreciation approximately $55 million for the first quarter and $218 million for full-year 2026; SG&A $153 million, plus or minus $2 million, held at that level each quarter of 2026. Management expects margin to improve through the year as ASP declines are front-loaded with the annual contracts and volume efficiencies and the Newport ramp kick in.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 guide: revenues between $800 million and $830 million; gross margin 19.9%, plus or minus 50 basis points; Newport drag 50 to 75 basis points

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 capex plan: between $400 million and $440 million, a bit more than half of it (around $230 million) for the 12-inch fab in Germany, including a carryover from 2025 after equipment deliveries slipped to Q1; nearly all 12-inch fab spend falls in the first half and marks the peak of the five-year capacity expansion plan. Other capacity spend targets the large DC power capacitor for smart grid (projects out to the year 2032), tantalum polymer capacitors ("used in AI, automotive, industrial") and power inductors expanding further in Mexico because customers want regional, non-tariff supply. Full-year 2025 capex came in below the $300 million to $350 million guidance because of the 12-inch equipment delay; Q4 capex was $95 million, including $75 million for capacity expansion. After the 2026 peak, capital intensity should return from nine and ten percent to the five and six percent levels, and 2026 free cash flow is again expected to be negative.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 capex between $400 million and $440 million; around $230 million for the 12-inch fab; Q4 capex $95 million ($75 million for capacity expansion)

quarterly_data.signal: Supply is tightening and pricing is firming: lead times are stretching for diodes and MOSFETs in both Asia and The Americas, customers are placing orders with longer visibility and looking to secure supply, and Asian distributors are also ordering ahead of the Lunar New Year. Vishay started increasing prices in October due to metals ("We were one of the first to do it"), raised prices on quite a few products in the fourth quarter effective from early Q1, and will come back with a second price increase in some product lines; the October-December annual contract negotiations produced a price decrease "much less than what was historical", so management sees 2026 ASP decline lower than historical. Distribution inventory dropped to 22 weeks from 23 weeks and POS increased 3%. Vishay used its expanded capacity to meet urgent automotive supply needs during the December shortages, gaining MOSFET and diode share, with the ramp beyond March depending on customer site audits.
quarterly_data.figure: distribution inventory dropped to 22 weeks from 23 weeks; POS increased 3%

quarterly_data.signal: Silicon carbide and solution selling: Vishay released eight Gen 2 1200 volt planar MOSFETs for industrial use and its first trench MOSFET, the silicon carbide Gen 3 1200 volts, for industrial and automotive applications, "positioning us to design in 800 volt automotive and AI applications"; trench samples now let customers qualify Vishay into 400 volt and 800 volt EV systems. Q4 also brought three new reference designs (a 40 amp bidirectional eFuse, a 20 amp unidirectional eFuse and an isolated current sensor for high voltage applications), promoting Vishay products populating 80% or more of the components on a circuit board in a power application. Newport keeps ramping wafer production with four automotive audits planned for Q1 (including two new customers), and the subcontractor initiative has qualified over 10,000 part numbers since it began two years ago.
quarterly_data.figure: eight Gen 2 1200 volt MOSFETs released; first silicon carbide Gen 3 1200 volts trench MOSFET; over 10,000 part numbers qualified

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 market view: asked whether the earlier industry expectation of mid to high single digits had changed, management said "The view is still mid to high single digits" - industrial power mid to high single digit, automotive flat to mid single digit for Vishay, aerospace defense mid to high single digit, AI mid to high single digit and healthcare mid single digits - and Vishay is pushing to outperform the market. These five growth markets represent about 95% of the core business. On rising memory prices, management said AI and compute consume far more memory than Vishay's industrial, automotive and aerospace defense segments, so it is "not forecasting a negative impact to revenue".
quarterly_data.figure: five growth markets represent about 95% of core business; AI growth view mid to high single digit
